8
A device for spraying paint consists of a box with its axes horizontal and vertical. One of its
vertical faces contains small holes. Paint is fed into the box under pressure via a vertical tube and
exits through the holes as fine streams moving horizontally.
paint in
paint out through holes
(only a few holes are shown)
The paint is ejected at a speed of 2.5 m s–1 through 400 holes, each of area 0.4 mm2. The density
of the paint is 900 kg m–3.
What is the horizontal force required to hold the device stationary as it ejects the paint?
A
0.36 N
B
0.90 N
C
2.3 N
D
900 N

hints: Notice the paint gains horizontal momentum from rest in the box to $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ through 400 holes, so the holding force must equal the rate of gain of momentum.
Connect volume flow to mass flow using density: mass per second $= \rho \times$ total area $\times$ speed, remembering $0.4 \text{ mm}^2 = 0.4 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$ for each hole.
First calculate total area for 400 holes and mass per second, then multiply that mass rate by $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to get $F = \Delta p/\Delta t$ in newtons.
walkthrough: Total exit area is needed because all 400 holes eject paint. $A = 400 \times 0.4 \text{ mm}^2 = 160 \text{ mm}^2 = 160 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2 = 1.6 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$.
Volume ejected per second is area times speed: $V/t = A v = 1.6 \times 10^{-4} \times 2.5 = 4.0 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^3 \text{ s}^{-1}$.
Mass ejected per second uses paint density $900 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$: $m/t = \rho V/t = 900 \times 4.0 \times 10^{-4} = 0.36 \text{ kg s}^{-1}$.

Horizontal force equals rate of change of horizontal momentum. Paint starts with negligible horizontal velocity in the box and leaves at $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so $F = (m/t) \times v = 0.36 \times 2.5$.
This gives $F = 0.90 \text{ N}$ opposite to the paint jets, which is the force needed to hold the device stationary. This is option B.

A.explanation: This is the mass ejected per second in $\text{kg s}^{-1}$, not the force. Force needs a further multiplication by the ejection speed $2.5 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Mass per second is $\rho A v$ and force is mass per second times $v$, giving $0.36 \times 2.5 = 0.90 \text{ N}$.

C.explanation: This value is too large and does not follow from $F = \rho A v^2$ with correct conversion of $0.4 \text{ mm}^2$ to $\text{m}^2$.

D.explanation: This confuses density $900 \text{ kg m}^{-3}$ with a force and ignores total hole area and the $v^2$ dependence of the thrust.
